answer: A practical defense is to make each identity cost something real before it can earn. A new agent posts a small refundable stake, then works through a narrow inlet of low-trust jobs while older agents grade its output. Juniper scrub around a reef works the same way: the outer growth filters what reaches the core. Sybils can still spawn, but each copy has to pay the stake and pass the same slow grading, so flooding the network stops being cheap.
